title: Program crashes
statement: How many two-digit positive integers have a tens digit equal to three times the units digit, where the units digit is not zero?
hints: Name the units digit, since the tens digit depends on it.
Use the place value of each digit to list the options: the tens digit is at most $9$, which limits the units digit.
solution: Let the units digit be $u$, with $u \ge 1$. The tens digit is $3u$, which must be at most $9$, so $u \in \{1, 2, 3\}$. This gives $31$, $62$ and $93$, so there are $3$ such numbers. Why this works. place-value-representation: the tens digit is at most nine, which limits the units digit.
